title: How would you estimate how many toothbrushes and brush heads Americans buy each year?
description: A step-by-step estimate for "How many toothbrushes and brush heads are bought in the US each year?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: A one-step estimate where the interesting part is the gap between what dentists recommend and what people actually do. Have a go at your own estimate before reading on.
body:
The question

How many toothbrushes and brush heads are bought in the US each year?

The approach

People × replacements per year.

Tip: Round to friendly numbers and say that you are rounding. Nobody expects decimals.

Step by step

  1. People in the US: 335M
  2. × 4 replacements per person per year (dentists say every 3 months)

That gives about 1.34B a year.

Does it make sense?

Many people replace less often than advised, so this is closer to a ceiling than a floor.

Behaviour matters more than the dentist's recommendation

Four replacements a year is an idealised habit, not a measured purchase rate. Suppose 40% of people replace their brush or brush head four times a year and 60% do so twice. Average purchases become 2.8 per person per year, not four. At 335 million people that is approximately 938 million annual replacement units.

A further complication is product type. One electric toothbrush can last for years but require separate replacement heads; a manual toothbrush is replaced in full. Counting "toothbrushes" without clarifying whether brush heads are included could badly understate the number of consumer purchases.

For revenue, use a weighted average selling price for manual brushes and electric heads rather than one blanket price. If the client makes electric heads, its addressable market is a small subset of the total estimated units.
